questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Wine experts and how price affects how wine tastes
How to make your own red and white wine at home
The long history of wine-making in France and Italy
Why people should stop drinking alcohol completely
questions.why: They discuss sommeliers and research showing price changes how much we like wine.

questions.q: How does Rob describe his relationship with wine?
options: He is an expert who knows a lot about it
He never drinks it
He only drinks expensive wine
He enjoys it but isn't an expert
questions.why: Rob says he isn't a connoisseur, 'although the enjoy part is true'.

questions.q: According to Rob, how can wine be useful even for people who don't drink alcohol?
options: It can be used for cooking special meals
It can be used as medicine
It can be an investment sold at auction
It can be given as a present
questions.why: Rob says wine can be a commodity you invest in and sell at an auction.

questions.q: What surprised Bianca Bosker about sommeliers?
options: They didn't really like the taste of wine
They made a pleasure into something painful
They earned very little money
They only drank cheap wine
questions.why: She says they turned wine into 'something approaching sheer God-awful pain'.

questions.q: Which of these did Bianca Bosker NOT say sommeliers did?
options: Licked rocks
Took dance classes
Hired memory coaches
Worked on farms growing grapes
questions.why: She mentions licking rocks, voice and memory coaches and dance classes, but not farm work.

questions.q: What is Rob's reaction to sommeliers divorcing their spouses?
options: He thinks it is a bit extreme
He thinks it shows real dedication
He wants to try the same training
He doesn't believe it is true
questions.why: Rob says divorcing their spouses 'does sound a bit extreme'.

questions.q: According to Hilke Plassmann, what does a higher price do?
options: It makes people drink less wine at dinner
It makes our brain really like the taste more
It has no effect on the taste
It makes people suspicious of the wine
questions.why: She says the price tag affects the brain region that encodes how much you like the taste.

questions.q: What advice does Sam give based on this research?
options: Always buy the most expensive wine
Only drink wine in restaurants
Tell yourself the cheaper option is fine
Ask a sommelier before buying
questions.why: Sam says it may be better telling yourself that the cheaper option is OK.
